sample_unit: standardized pediatric discharge instructions (each translated into 3 languages by 3 sources)

links.outcome: Potentially clinically significant translation errors (severity score ≤3) for Haitian Creole versus professional translation
links.effect: Haitian Creole errors: ChatGPT 33.3% (P < .001), Google Translate 23.3% (P = .024), professional translations 8.3%.
links.quote: ChatGPT (33.3%, P < .001) and Google Translate (23.3%, P = .024) contained more potentially clinically significant errors (severity score ≤3) for Haitian Creole than professional translations (8.3%).

links.outcome: Translation quality (adequacy, fluency, meaning, severity) compared with professional translations, by language
links.effect: Machine translation was comparable to professional translation for Spanish and Portuguese but significantly worse for Haitian Creole on adequacy, fluency, meaning, and severity.
links.quote: Machine translation platforms have comparable performance to professional translations for Spanish and Portuguese but shortcomings in quality, accuracy, and preference persist for Haitian Creole.

unlisted_practices: Using professional human translation rather than machine translation for low-resource languages such as Haitian Creole

screen.reason: Evaluated the translation quality and clinical harm risk of ChatGPT and Google Translate compared to professional translation for pediatric discharge instructions without testing a specific organizational deployment safeguard.
